correctness.rationale: Exact hub and petal update equations are reconstructed in RESULT.md. In odd petal counts an invertible sum/difference change of variables isolates a four-dimensional block B with B^3=I, fixed dimension 2, and k-1 size-three Jordan blocks. In even petal counts a different invertible change isolates a seven-dimensional block C with ranks of powers of C+I equal to 4,3,2,1,0, and k-2 size-three blocks. These force the claimed all-k similarity type. Fixed-power dimensions, Möbius inversion, exact orders and maximal-period fractions follow with correct boundary k=1. Distinct microscopic and algebraic programs were run from included source and agreed on 74,896 fully enumerated states (k=1..5) and all fixed-power nullities (k=1..12). Finite checks corroborate but are not offered as infinite proof.

value.rationale: A mathematically motivated infinite graph family (multiple simple 4-cycles joined at one cutvertex) exhibits a sharp parity-dependent structural effect when using the same reversible local rule: odd k creates an irreducible cubic temporal factor plus J3 modes, whereas even k has one J5 mode; this switches the maximum possible period from 12 to 8. An explicit similarity classification gives all primitive-period populations and nontrivial positive maximal-period fractions (one-half versus asymptotic three-quarters), not merely isolated computations. The hub-coupling mechanism is a structural statement that is reusable in sequential graph dynamics.
